html:
The Vedic Aryans were speakers of an early Indo-Aryan language, the ancestor of Sanskrit, who lived in north-western and then northern India from about 1500 BCE. The map shows them from 1500 to 700 BCE. Their age is the Vedic period.

They called themselves arya, "noble". They came into the Punjab from the north-west as part of the Indo-Aryan migrations, bringing horses, chariots and a language related to Persian, Greek and Latin. At first they were cattle herders in tribes, led by chiefs and served by priests. Their hymns, collected in the Rigveda, were passed on by memory with great precision for centuries before being written down.

Around 1200 to 1000 BCE they moved east into the Ganges plain, took up iron tools, cleared forest and settled as farmers. Tribes combined into kingdoms such as the Kuru realm, where the rules of Vedic ritual and the varna order of priests, warriors, commoners and servants took shape. By about 600 BCE their world had grown into the kingdoms and cities of the Mahajanapadas. They mixed with the Dravidian and other peoples already there.
